reference: For large values of d, additive attention outperforms scaled dot-product attention without scaling. This is because, as the values of k increase, the dot products grow large in magnitude, which can push the softmax function into regions where it has extremely small gradients. To counteract this effect, scaled dot-product attention scales the dot products by the square root of d. Multi-head attention benefits from this by performing several attention layers in parallel, allowing it to project queries, keys, and values into different dimensions and compute the attention function simultaneously.

reference: Multi-Head Attention enhances the performance of the Transformer model by allowing it to draw global dependencies between input and output without relying on recurrence. This mechanism enables the model to compute representations of sequences more efficiently, as it reduces the number of operations required to relate signals from distant positions to a constant number. In contrast, traditional recurrent networks face challenges in learning dependencies over long distances due to their sequential nature. The use of Multi-Head Attention allows for parallelization and significantly improves translation quality, achieving state-of-the-art results in a shorter training time.

reference: In the architecture of the Transformer model, the multi-head self-attention mechanism is a crucial component of both the encoder and decoder stacks. In the encoder, each layer consists of a multi-head self-attention mechanism as the first sub-layer, which allows the model to focus on different parts of the input sequence simultaneously. In the decoder, a third sub-layer is added that performs multi-head attention over the output of the encoder stack, enabling the decoder to incorporate information from the encoder while generating predictions. This design facilitates better contextual understanding and improves the overall performance of the model.
